author: agent:claude-code
message: Housecleaning the declared checks: eight were failing in 0.3-0.5 s because their commands carried CI-era prose or wouldn't run outside CI; each corrected command was run here first (except where noted). Plus the misstep that broke this machine's stable toolchain while doing it.

title: Adding a target to rust-toolchain.toml broke vghydra's stable toolchain
body: Adding wasm32-wasip1 to rust-toolchain.toml's targets (2026-11-09) made the next cargo call sync the toolchain. With `channel = "stable"` that meant updating stable 1.98.1 to 1.99.1, not just adding a target: rustup removed every component, then failed to install (a partial rust-std-wasm32-wasip1 already on disk was a conflict, and its rollback couldn't rename share/ back), leaving stable without rustc. Stable is the machine default, so every project without its own pin broke with it. The change was reverted; repairing stable (uninstall and reinstall) is the user's to run. Lesson: an edit to rust-toolchain.toml is a toolchain install, and on a floating channel an upgrade of the machine's default too; make it on its own, with nothing else running cargo, and check `rustup toolchain list` and `rustc --version` straight after. A pinned version (rule rust.toolchain-pinned) would have limited it to adding the target.

title: Miri rounds float operations at random
body: Under Miri, four tests that compare two routes bit for bit failed (dynamic::ops functions_reductions_and_casts: |3+4i| = 4.999998; the two dynamic::processor runtime-typed tests; signal::ndarray's strided-axis test): Miri gives each float operation (sqrt, hypot, sin and the rest) a random rounding error, so the same computation twice differs. No undefined behaviour was reported. With MIRIFLAGS=-Zmiri-deterministic-floats all four pass. `cargo xtask miri` sets that flag (tend runs a check through pwsh on Windows and sh elsewhere, so an inline environment variable isn't portable).
